description: Both: more supply of a product (flour delivery / unsold tyres) does not end scarcity; same reasoning, different object. V:1.1-002-WHY and V:1.1-003-APP also cover 'not removed by plenty/income'.
recommendation: Keep V:1.1-010; drop J:1.1-007 (carries 'invented Tsumeb' meta-language and adds no new reasoning).

description: Opportunity cost = next-best forgone, not difference/both. V uses money (N$480 vs 350), J uses ranked non-money options (revised ranking 1-3).
recommendation: Keep both: different representation (monetary vs ranked), good transfer pair.

description: Four V items ask for a judgement on 'use scarce slot/budget for A vs B and name OC'. 009 (training vs N$480 job) is a flashcard-sized version of P01(b)/P04.
recommendation: Move 1.1-009 to the assessment bank; keep P01, P03, P04 only if scenarios differ (they do: radio, shelters/footpath, mobile library).

description: Same judgement (central plan/public provision vs private/mixed for basic water or services) appears in V P04, J 017 (7m card), J P03 case 1 and J P02 (all use the same N$6,000 / one team water-point stem).
recommendation: Keep V:1.2-P04 (distinct: region, information problem) and J:1.2-P03; remove J:1.2-017-EVAL as flashcard (move to task bank or drop; its content is Case 1 of J:1.2-P03).

description: Both classify/describe a mixed system via private operation + public finance.
recommendation: Keep J:1.2-015 (4m, explains allocation mechanism); drop V:1.2-006 (2m, subset).

description: Progression: V states difference in coordination; J 011/013 require the mechanism (price/profit signal vs plan instruction).
Four near-identical 'Define X system' cards; different terms, no duplicate. 1.2-016 (mixed) answer wording is thin compared with revised 014/015 (private ownership / state ownership clause).
recommendation: Keep; unify the ownership/allocation clause across 014-016 (see contradictions).

description: V P03(c) (fish-drying cluster, further concentration) = J 012 (regional food-processing, volatile demand). V P04 (export-crop concentration) = J 014 (national specialisation, overseas demand changes).
recommendation: Remove J:1.3-012-EVAL and J:1.3-014-EVAL as flashcards (duplicate judgement already assessed in V P03/P04); keep J:1.3-010-EVAL (individual worker, unique).

description: Classification of examples is the application of the three level definitions.
Practice/familiarity vs reduced task-switching: two different mechanisms behind higher output per hour.
Identify 'single individual unincorporated' and 'members owning for shared interests' = recall of the two V definitions in reverse direction.
recommendation: Drop J:2.1-003 (no added reasoning beyond defs and V:2.1-P03).

description: Mirror pair: private mine (primary activity, private ownership) vs government factory (secondary activity, public ownership) - ownership vs activity classification.
Three finance/control trade-off judgements (partner; convert to private company with investor; public share offer vs investors).
recommendation: Keep; J 020 needs 'Copper Acacia'/'Invented' meta-text removed.

description: Cross-topic: private vs public sector definition; J 2.1-001 (revised) says 'owned and controlled', V 6.1-001 'owned or controlled'.
recommendation: Keep one definition of public sector (see contradictions); J:2.1-001 retained as the contrast card, V:6.1-001 can stay if wording aligned.

description: Scarce specialist skills strengthen union bargaining; J adds strong output demand and replacement difficulty.
021 (guesthouse owners = employers' association, not union) and 025 (factory owners' body not a union) test the same representation-side distinction.
Both evaluate whether workers should join/form a union with subscriptions as the cost and weak communication/transport as the benefit.
recommendation: Keep V:2.2-P04 as task; move 2.2-018 to assessment bank or drop (duplicates P04 judgement).

description: Union settlement/bargaining strength depends on firm's demand (rising vs falling orders; weak demand + many applicants).
Employers' association helps members (collective training need vs pooled advice for small firms).
V:2.3-P02 parts (c) price label/store of value, (f) debit card, (a)/(b) definitions repeat card prompts word for word in substance.
recommendation: Remove V:2.3-P02 from assessment bank (see assessment_tasks); cards already cover.

description: Five cards on 'depreciation raises domestic cost of a fixed foreign-currency bill' (importer, buyer, fixed 20 units, US$50, US$100 input).
recommendation: Keep V:2.3-009 (4m interpretation), J:2.3-012 (conversion calc), J:7.4-004 (third-currency N$18->20). Drop V:2.3-012-CHAIN (subset of 009) and V:2.3-010-APP (units bought, same direction).

description: J:2.3-P03 two cases reuse J 018/017 (commercial-bank account/credit; stock exchange for equity) and J 016 (central bank).
recommendation: Keep the three 7m EVAL as assessment items; drop J:2.3-P03 (14m two-case) or rewrite with fresh scenarios.

description: Function vs quality distinction taught (V), then applied (J 003) and listing functions (J 005).
Remote order (repair booking / bag by message) is a market because buyer-seller contact is arranged.
Digital + physical channel combined (tailor, uniform repair, Pebble Pots).
recommendation: Keep, but 3.1 is 0.2% of examined marks and has 4 tasks+7 cards: over-weighted; do not add more.

description: Same input-cost supply decrease on the same bread-roll schedule (N$8/80 -> N$10/60) once as diagram, once as written interpretation.
Supply increase and new equilibrium (J roll schedule, V seed/packet diagram). J 009 and 015/016 are mirror directions of the same dataset.
Lower production cost (technology / cheaper flour) shifts supply right, price down, quantity up.
recommendation: Keep J:3.2-013 (4m with equilibrium effect); drop V:3.2-012.

description: Supply left: crop failure (price/quantity effects) vs flour cost rise (shift only).
Own-price change = movement along curve, not a shift (V 004 snack; J 018 'control selects a price on existing curves').
recommendation: Keep V:3.2-004 (clear, no dataset dependency); J:3.2-018 depends on the roll dataset - keep only if dataset restated per card.

description: V:3.2-P01 is numerically identical to card 010 (D 90/60/30 -> 120/90/60, S 30/60/90, N$10/20/30); same supply/demand base as 006 and 017.
recommendation: Change P01 numbers (see template_reuse); otherwise a learner who did card 010 already holds the answer to P01(b).

description: V:3.2-P02 (8 x 2 marks) restates cards: (a) equilibrium price, (b) own-price change, (c/d) determinants, (e) brand vs category.
recommendation: Remove V:3.2-P02 as an assessment item.

description: All use the same Erongo Oven Stall roll schedule: P01 asks equilibrium, 007 asks imbalance, P02 repeats shift analysis; seven J cards/tasks on one dataset.
recommendation: Keep dataset for at most 3 items (007, 015, P02); replace rest with fresh markets.

description: Calculate PED from price and quantity change using original values. V result 1.5 (elastic), J result 0.5 (inelastic).
recommendation: Keep both: complementary elastic/inelastic outcomes; but unify sign convention (see contradictions).

description: Calculate PES; V 0.5, J 2.

Each calc card is followed by an interpretation card using the same numbers (12%/8%; 5%/10%; 5%/10%; 20%/10%): legitimate progression, but the interpretation answer is fully determined by the calc answer.
recommendation: Keep pairs; make the interpretation card state the coefficient without requiring recalculation (already the case) so it tests meaning, not repeat arithmetic.

description: J 001 (revised: state PED and PES formulas) is already contained in the V definitions, which print the formula.
Coefficient is a ratio not a percentage / why percentages: V P02(c) repeats 008; 021 is the reasoning behind it.
J uses one dataset (N$10->11, 100->95: PED 0.5, revenue N$1,000->1,045) in five selected items.
recommendation: Keep 006 and P02; template risk, see template_reuse.

description: Advertising purposes: 002 (revised to 'two reasons a business advertises') restates 007 (define purpose: inform/persuade...).
Poster for local passers-by: J informative purpose; V local vs distant campaign method choice.
Distinction card after two definitions.
recommendation: Keep 007/008; 005 is optional (answer is a concatenation of 007+008) - low value, drop if capacity is needed.

description: Monopoly lower unit cost vs price paid by consumers (V sole supplier; J N$9/N$10 vs N$6/N$12) judged five times.
recommendation: Remove V:3.5-003-EVAL and J:3.5-005-EVAL as flashcards; keep V:3.5-P04, J:3.5-P02, J:3.5-P03 (two cases) only if J:3.5-P02 numbers differ from P03.

description: Two definitions then differences between them.
Wage vs non-wage factors: defs 004/005, distinction 002, application J 003 (basic pay vs journey time). 002 is a concatenation of 004+005.
recommendation: Drop V:4.1-002; keep J:4.1-003 as application.

description: Both: moving town with the same occupation shows geographical, not occupational, mobility (retagged J 4.2-021 to 4.1).
Compare job offers: non-wage may outweigh N$500 (V); net of travel cost N$200 advantage (J); hourly x hours (V P01).
Transfer earnings/economic rent: two definitions, one distinction, two worked splits (6,000/5,000 and 8,000/6,000), a P03(b) 10,000/8,000 and J P01 7,000 - seven items on one skill.
recommendation: Drop J:4.2-019-DIST (V defs cover it) and V:4.2-020-MISCON (J:4.2-020-APP and P03(b) cover the numeric split); keep J:4.2-022-MISCON (different misconception: transfer payment).

description: Scarce skill + strong demand -> higher pay (V 2m; J three 4m variants: repair vs packing; private clinic vs public; widening gap).
recommendation: Keep J:4.2-007 and J:4.2-017; drop V:4.2-002 (subset); J:4.2-009 optional.

description: Three 'averages mislead' cards (sector averages mix occupations; composition raises average; group average overlap).
Cross-topic: subtracting tax gives disposable income, not real income. V 4.2-019 is taught before price index (7.1).
Real income vs nominal: 10% pay rise with index 100->110; 10% inflation on fixed pension; unchanged income buys less.
recommendation: Keep V:4.2-009 and J:7.1-007 (numbers); drop V:7.1-009-CHAIN (qualitative restatement).

description: Same hourly rate, different earnings (hours); gender-gap decomposition; discrimination when hours equal.
Budget-share comparison of N$3,000 vs N$9,000 households; both banks chose the same two incomes.
recommendation: Keep V:4.3-003 and J:4.3-001, vary incomes in tasks (see template_reuse).

description: Borrowing: not free income (V) -> N$1,000 principal/N$100 interest -> urgent roof repair motives -> low income, strong need but limited credit.
More income need not mean more saving / larger savings balance is a stock not willingness.
recommendation: Keep J:4.3-004 and V:4.3-P04; drop V:4.3-P02 (bundle).

description: Higher revenue/output does not mean higher profit (A 6,000 vs B 5,000; manual 6,000 vs machine 5,000; 30 batches N$400 vs 20 batches N$500).
recommendation: Keep 003 and J 001 (evaluation, but see assessment_tasks); P01 repeats the 003 pattern with new figures - acceptable as transfer.

description: Same pottery numbers (7,000/6,200/9,000) in a card, a data task and an essay.
recommendation: Keep card 006; refresh numbers in P02/P03.

description: Derived demand: cheaper machine not demanded (task fit) vs machine raises maintenance labour demand (complements).
Revenue rise may not raise profit vs profit rise is not maximised profit.
Output doubles/falls but productivity (ratio) unchanged; J 010 adds illness absence.
HIV/illness: effect depends on actual illness, not status. Repeated in 5.2 (V, J) and 6.3 (V).
recommendation: Keep J:5.2-009 (4m); drop V:5.2-015-CHAIN; keep V:6.3-015 (employer inference) only.

description: Training raises productivity -> training alone limited when equipment is the bottleneck.
Cross-topic 'Define total revenue' twice with different wording.
recommendation: Keep one wording; V:3.3-004 stays in 3.3 (needed there) and V:5.3-023 may be dropped or made 'Define average revenue's numerator'.

description: Average revenue vs marginal revenue.
Same data (120 produced, 100 sold, N$8): calculate then expose the units-produced error.
Tile manufacturer buys clay supplier: J 007 identifies backward integration, J 021 explains error of calling it forward - same scenario and conclusion.
recommendation: Drop J:5.4-007; keep J:5.4-021 and V:5.4-029 (direction relative to focal firm).

description: Net AC effect (3 saving, 1 coordination) is also the opening data of J P02.
Limited demand/owner preference limits firm size.
recommendation: Drop J:5.4-016 (V P04 and V 015 cover).

description: LRAC data interpretation: 12->8 (total cost rises), 6->7, six-factory curve, 6->5 doubling.
Ten near-identical definition cards; each term distinct, but 025 (risk-bearing) is worded 'potential cost advantages' instead of 'reductions in LRAC' like the other five types.
Identify producer/employer roles (J) after defining them (V).
Proportional tax: 10% of N$4,000/N$10,000 vs 10% of N$2,000/N$6,000.
Equal cash levy (N$100 on N$1,000/5,000; N$200 on N$2,000/6,000) falls as a share of income = regressive, not proportional.
Fiscal vs monetary: mirror misconceptions; J 014 (identify categories) adds nothing beyond V 024/025 definitions and these two cards.
Six interest-rate transmission items (firm credit-financed purchase; generic lending-rate rise; 8%->10% on N$100,000; weak sales; customers on credit; revised V 018 saver).
recommendation: Keep J:6.2-032 (calculation), J:6.2-018 (limitation), V:6.2-018 (revised: saver, different direction); drop J:6.2-017 (restates V:6.2-017) and V:6.2-017 or J:6.2-017 - retain one.

description: 'Real total rises but per-person average does not' appears five times across 6.2, 7.3, 8.2 (0%, 4% vs 6%, 5% vs 8%, 5% vs 5%, 10% vs 20%).
recommendation: Keep V:8.2-014 and J:8.2-009 in 8.2 (the syllabus home); keep V:6.2-034 in 6.2; drop J:6.2-009 and V:7.3-009.

description: Budget deficit calculation vs confusing it with trade deficit.
Cross-topic: goods trade balance is not the whole balance of payments (J zero goods balance; V goods deficit).
Falling positive inflation does not mean falling prices appears as J 6.2-007 and as part (d) of V 7.1-P02.
recommendation: Keep J:6.2-007 (or relocate to 7.1); drop V:7.1-P02 task.

description: Mirror: expand demand with constrained capacity raises prices; restrain demand limits inflation.
001 (safety rule makes firm correct hazard), 005 (standard changes method), 011 (inspection leads to correction): three cards on the same rule->compliance->less injury chain.
Diagram: ceiling (shortage), floor (surplus), minimum wage (unemployment): one skill in three markets.
recommendation: Keep 017 and 019 (goods vs labour); 018 is optional transfer.

description: Minimum wage above vs below market wage: complementary.
Inflation and borrowers: V 010 (revised) says borrowers repay with less valuable money; J 008 and V P04 qualify with income/interest terms.
recommendation: Drop V:7.1-010 (also contradicts the qualified stance, see contradictions).

description: Cost-push from imported inputs with unchanged demand/nominal pay.
Calculate index (110) then interpret points vs per cent (120->126).
Level rises but share falls (agriculture 200->220 of 500->600; manufacturing 200->240 of 1,000->1,500).
recommendation: Keep J 001 card; V P01 and J P02 repeat with new numbers.

description: Match remedy to cause of unemployment (skills vs demand vs season).
recommendation: Keep V:7.2-P04 or J:7.2-P03 (both assess same matching judgement); keep cards.

description: Unemployment rate denominator (600/100/300) then discouraged workers.
Value-added chain: V 60/100/160 appears in card 006 and again in P03; J 100/250 in revised card 010 and J P02.
Revised J 008 asks to name three methods and what each adds = the three V definitions.
Exports included, imports excluded: stated in V 015 formula (X-M) and P02(f).
Real series separates output change from price change for policy assessment.
recommendation: Keep J:7.3-015 (4m); drop V:7.3-008 (revised to 'one reason government measures national income').

description: GNP = GDP + income received - paid abroad (485; 815).
Six V items on one dataset (A 30C/15G, B 12C/12G): 007 contains 010 (absolute) and 013 (comparative) combined; P03(b) repeats.
OC calc (12 mats/6 baskets) -> B can still gain -> comparative advantage misconception.
Goods balance: define -> compute deficit 20 -> deficit widens although exports rise -> not whole BoP.
Natural vs total population change: concept (V 008), numeric misconception (V 017), full calc (J 008).
Larger working-age group raises output only with skills, jobs, equipment; mirror framing (not automatically / when conditions met).
recommendation: Drop J:8.1-018 (card) and keep V:8.1-012; keep P04 and J P03 only one if tasks are rationalised.

description: TFR: definition then interpretation of 2.5 (not per year).
Average income (per head) hides distribution/access: six selected cards/tasks make the same point (sanitation, water, individual income).
recommendation: Keep J:8.2-003 (4m analysis) and V:8.2-005 (within-country disparity); drop V:8.2-002-DIST and J:8.2-001-DIST.

description: Per-head real income: total +5% and population +5% (unchanged) vs +10% and +20% (falls).
Private vs external benefit/cost (J revised to label profit and garden damage).
recommendation: Keep V:9.1-004 (definition); drop J:9.1-001 or merge as example.

description: Reed harvest larger vs managed (003) and ban vs monitored lower harvest (004): same managed-use judgement; V 003 resource project with lasting harm; J P03 Case 1 repeats.
Tariff with review date and tax-funded path: J EVAL cards are Cases 2/3 of J:9.1-P03; V P03/P04 cover tariff and public provision.
recommendation: Keep V P03/P04 and J 002; remove J:9.1-005 and J:9.1-006 as flashcards (move to tasks only if P03 is dropped).

description: Quota is not a tariff: 011's answer is the conjunction of 012 and 013.
Social cost = private + external: J N$8,000 + 5,000; V N$80,000 + 20,000.
Five 'Define A versus B' compound cards (two definitions in one 2-mark card): each answer needs two separate definitions for 1 mark each.
recommendation: Split or reword so each card has one concept (see contradictions/language).
